How Do I Tell If the High Temperatures Are Hurting My Yard?

Lowcountry summers are beautiful, but the combination of high temperatures, humidity, intense sunlight, and inconsistent rainfall can put serious stress on your landscape.

Sometimes the signs are obvious. Other times, your lawn and plants may be struggling long before they start turning brown.

So, how can you tell if the heat is hurting your yard?

Here are some of the most common signs to watch for.

1. Your Grass Is Turning Brown or Yellow

Discoloration is one of the easiest signs of heat stress to spot.

Look for:

  • Brown or yellow patches
  • Thinning grass
  • Dry, brittle blades
  • Bare spots
  • Grass that doesn’t bounce back after being walked on

Some warm-season grasses naturally slow down or go dormant during periods of extreme heat and drought. However, widespread or uneven discoloration could also indicate irrigation problems, insects, disease, or soil issues.

Before increasing your watering, it’s important to determine what’s actually causing the problem.

2. Your Soil Is Extremely Dry

Check the soil around your lawn and landscape beds.

If the soil is extremely dry, hard, or pulling away from surrounding surfaces, your plants may not be getting enough moisture.

This is particularly important for:

  • Newly installed plants
  • Newly planted trees
  • New sod
  • Container plants
  • Plants in full afternoon sun

A properly functioning irrigation system can help provide consistent moisture, but watering needs vary depending on your soil, plants, weather, and landscape conditions.

3. Your Plants Are Wilting

Wilting leaves are another common sign of heat stress.

You may notice:

  • Drooping leaves
  • Curling leaves
  • Leaves losing their normal color
  • Premature leaf drop
  • Plants looking tired during the hottest part of the day

Some plants naturally wilt temporarily during extreme afternoon heat and recover later in the evening.

However, if plants remain wilted even after temperatures drop, they may be experiencing more serious stress.

4. Leaves Are Turning Brown Around the Edges

Have you noticed brown, crispy edges on your plants?

This can be a sign of leaf scorch or heat stress.

It’s particularly common when plants are exposed to intense sunlight, dry conditions, or inconsistent watering.

Don’t automatically assume the plant needs more water. Leaf damage can have multiple causes, including:

  • Heat
  • Drought
  • Root problems
  • Poor soil conditions
  • Excessive fertilizer
  • Disease

If you’re unsure, it’s best to have the plant evaluated before changing your maintenance routine.

5. Your Trees Are Showing Signs of Stress

Trees are generally more resilient than smaller plants, but extreme heat can still affect them, especially newly planted trees or trees already experiencing health problems.

Watch for:

  • Wilting foliage
  • Brown leaf edges
  • Premature leaf drop
  • Dead branches
  • Sparse canopy growth
  • Cracked or damaged limbs

Large mature trees should receive particular attention when they’re located near your home, driveway, pool, fence, or outdoor living space.

If you notice dead or damaged branches, a professional tree inspection can help determine whether trimming or additional care is needed.

6. Some Areas of Your Yard Look Healthy While Others Don’t

If one part of your lawn looks great while another area is brown, don’t assume the entire lawn has a problem.

Uneven lawn health can be a sign of:

  • Broken sprinkler heads
  • Clogged irrigation nozzles
  • Poor irrigation coverage
  • Compacted soil
  • Drainage problems
  • Different amounts of sunlight

This is one reason checking your irrigation system during periods of extreme heat is so important.

Run your system and watch it operate. Are all zones receiving water? Are sprinkler heads functioning properly? Is water reaching the areas that need it?

7. Newly Planted Landscaping Is Struggling

New landscaping is especially vulnerable during high temperatures.

Recently planted trees, shrubs, flowers, and sod haven’t had enough time to establish extensive root systems.

If you’ve recently invested in landscape installation or tree planting, pay close attention to signs of stress.

New plants may require more consistent watering than established plants, particularly during extended periods of high temperatures.

8. Your Mulch Is Dry or Has Washed Away

Mulch helps protect plant roots and retain moisture, but it can become less effective when it’s extremely thin or has been washed away by heavy summer rain.

Check your landscape beds for:

  • Exposed soil
  • Thin mulch
  • Washed-out areas
  • Increased weeds
  • Dry soil around plants

Refreshing your mulch can help improve moisture retention and give your landscape beds a cleaner appearance.

Just remember: don’t pile mulch against tree trunks or plant stems.

Don’t Just Add More Water

One of the biggest mistakes homeowners make during extreme heat is assuming that every problem is caused by insufficient watering.

More water isn’t always the answer.

Overwatering can contribute to:

  • Root problems
  • Fungal issues
  • Nutrient deficiencies
  • Poor plant health
  • Water waste

The goal is proper watering, not simply more watering.

An efficient irrigation system combined with the right watering schedule can help your landscape handle periods of extreme heat.

What Can You Do to Help Your Yard?

If your landscape is showing signs of heat stress, start by:

  • ✔️ Checking your irrigation system
  • ✔️ Inspecting soil moisture
  • ✔️ Watching newly planted landscaping closely
  • ✔️ Maintaining proper mulch levels
  • ✔️ Avoiding excessive fertilizer during stressful conditions
  • ✔️ Inspecting trees for damage
  • ✔️ Addressing drainage problems
  • ✔️ Monitoring your lawn regularly

And remember: some heat-related damage takes time to appear.

A plant may look fine during a heat wave and begin showing stress days later.

When Should You Call a Professional?

If you’re unsure what’s causing the problem, or if your landscape is declining quickly, it may be time to have a professional take a look.

Professional landscape and irrigation services can help identify whether the problem is related to water, soil, plant selection, insects, disease, drainage, or heat stress.

For trees, particularly large trees or those near structures, professional evaluation is especially important.

Keep Your Lowcountry Landscape Healthy Through the Heat

High temperatures are a normal part of life in Bluffton, Hilton Head, Okatie, Beaufort, and the surrounding Lowcountry.

Your landscape doesn’t have to suffer through them.

With proper lawn care, irrigation, tree maintenance, mulch, plant selection, and landscape maintenance, you can help your outdoor space stay healthier and more resilient throughout the summer.
